To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IB4-positive neurons are not a uniform population of sensory neurons, but are divided into two groups, one being NGF-dependent and the other GDNF-dependent.
many NGF/GDNFs-dependent neurons in the rat DRGs are labeled by isolectins, and that somatostatin mRNA is exclusively expressed in the IB4-positive neurons.
many NGF/GDNF/GDNFs-dependent neurons, including peptidergics, were labeled by isolectins B4 in rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationships between IB4 binding and expression of the NGF and GDNF receptor mRNAs in rat and mouse DRG neurons.
the relationships between IB4-binding neurons, trkA and/or c-ret mRNA-expressed neurons, and peptidergs in rat DRG.
the relationship between the isolectin B 4 (IB4)-positive neurons and the neurons expressing the neurotrophin receptors and neuropeptides in the rat sensory ganglia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IB4-positive DRG neurons include NGF/GDNF/GDNFs-dependent neurons, but that the majority of the NGF/GDNFs/GDNFs-dependent sensory neurons are not labeled by IB4.
the IB4-binding DRG neurons are heterogeneous, and include both NGF/GDNF-dependent and non-dependent neurons.
IB4-labeled DRG neurons are not NGF-dependent and non-peptidergic neurons but are NGF-dependent, peptidergics, and GDNF-dependent, non-peptidergetic neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

IB4-positive sensory neurons are not a homogeneous population, but are composed of two distinct groups: one is a small-sized, NGF/GDNF-dependent and somatostatin-containing population, and the other is a large-sized, c-ret/GDNF/GDNFs-dependent population.
the IB4-binding DRG neurons in rats are composed of the NGF-dependent and GDNF/GDNFs-dependent neurons.
the majority of IB4-binding neurons express trkA and/or c-ret mRNA and are NGF/GDNFs-dependent and peptidergic neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the IB4-labeled DRG neurons are not all non-neuronal growth factor-dependent, and that the intensely IB4-stained small neurons are NGF-dependent and non-peptidergic, and the weakly IB4-stained large neurons are GDNF-dependent and pepticergic.
the IB4-binding DRG neurons are heterogeneous with respect to the neurotrophic factors they depend on and the neuropeptides they synthesize.
IB4 is not specific for peptidergics.
